handbuch.seite.untertitel: Everything you need to know to play, in short chapters.
handbuch.suche.leer: Nothing in the handbook about that. Try another word.
handbuch.erste_schritte.kurz: The game and CalcioM work together: save, read in, close the day.
handbuch.erste_schritte.was: CalcioM accompanies your game. You keep playing in the game itself, CalcioM reads your save and builds the world in which you experience training, transfers, conversations and media.
handbuch.erste_schritte.ablauf:
Enter the folder of your game once, tap Check, then Remember.
Choose Read again. CalcioM backs up first, then reads your save and checks the result. This takes about half a minute.
Plan your day in CalcioM: training, conversations, offers. Everything is noted down.
Tap Continue. You see what is noted down and confirm with Confirm and put into the game.
Advance a day in the game or play the match, and save in the game. CalcioM recognises the new state by itself and processes the day.
At the end it says Done, and you land in the inbox.
handbuch.erste_schritte.wirkung: Putting into the game means: what you noted down in CalcioM is handed to the game. This mainly concerns your own squad: abilities, form and fitness, contracts, transfers, line-up and tactics. Form and fitness only go in shortly before a match, because the game keeps resetting them itself.
handbuch.erste_schritte.mehr:
Much of it deliberately stays in CalcioM only: the manager's private account, sponsors, tickets and stadium building, media, newspaper, diary and the board's trust. It always says there that nothing goes into the game.
If you skip several days at once, CalcioM works through every day in between. New deadlines only start on the target day, so you are not punished retroactively.
Before every read-in CalcioM makes a backup. Under Save and career you can take back the last day.
handbuch.erste_schritte.tipps:
Save in the game before you click on in CalcioM. Otherwise CalcioM misses the latest state.
If something hangs, everything stays noted down. The status bar shows whether all changes have arrived.
The inbox tells you when the game did not accept a change.
handbuch.inbox.kurz: Everything that needs you lands in the inbox as a case.
handbuch.inbox.was: Every topic is a case with a sender, a reason, deadlines and possible replies: an unhappy player, an offer, a board meeting, a report. All conversations run here too.
handbuch.inbox.ablauf:
Open the inbox. The tabs sort by decisions, conversations, negotiations, reports and media.
Pick a case and read what it is about and by when you should reply.
Choose a reply. Each option shows its intent, tone and a preview of the effect.
Your counterpart reacts. Depending on how it goes, another round follows or the conversation is closed.
handbuch.inbox.wirkung: Replies change mood, relationship, board trust, fan mood or media image. Some conversations cost money. A promise made in a conversation becomes a commitment you will be measured against later.
handbuch.inbox.mehr:
You get four to six options per round. There is always a way out and a constructive way. Some options are locked and name the reason, such as a lack of strength in your position.
Tone matters: warm, factual and praise go down well, hard and evasive annoy. How much depends on the character of your counterpart.
After about four replies a partner loses patience. An open conversation lapses after a week.
handbuch.inbox.tipps:
Anyone who waits long for a word from you gets unhappy. Answer player concerns promptly.
Pressure only works if your position is strong. Otherwise it costs mood.
Choosing the same option again has a weaker effect.
handbuch.transfers.kurz: Buy, sell, loan: how a move comes about.
handbuch.transfers.was: The area has three places. The Transfer Market is where you search for players and keep your transfer targets, loans and rumours. Negotiations shows everything in progress: talks, offers, completed deals and your contracts. Scouting is where your scouts work. On the transfer market you negotiate with clubs and players. Moves happen in summer from 1 July to 31 August and in winter in January. Offers from other clubs for your players are in the inbox.
handbuch.transfers.ablauf:
Shortlist a player or open him from scouting.
Make an offer and set fee and contract.
The assessment of the offer shows three bars: club, player and overall. The overall bar is never higher than the weaker of the two.
Talk to the player or his agent if his attitude does not fit yet.
Before signing comes the medical check.
The move counts once you save in the game and the day changes.
handbuch.transfers.wirkung: A move changes squad, wage bill and morale. Fans and media react to big sales and expensive signings. Loans know a fee, a purchase option and an obligation to buy.
handbuch.transfers.mehr:
The bars are a chance, not a promise. There are five levels from hopeless via open to certain.
The club usually asks for more than market value, clearly more for regulars. Far below that it refuses without a counter-offer.
The player has an attitude between wants it badly and wants to stay. Wage, playing time, role and ambition decide it. No player is sold against his will.
The medical check ends with passed, conspicuous or failed. With a finding you can renegotiate, go ahead anyway or call it off. Without an answer the deal collapses after three days.
Things can happen during a negotiation: an agent hesitates, a rival steps in, on the last day of the window events pile up. A player with a transfer request may go on strike.
handbuch.transfers.tipps:
Check the player's attitude before you bid a lot of fee.
With a conspicuous medical check a price reduction is often better than calling it off.
Only as many negotiations run at once as you set in the options.
handbuch.scouting.kurz: How well you really know a player depends on your scouts.
handbuch.scouting.was: Scouting gives you overview, assignments, scouts and reports in one place. Scouts watch players and deliver reports. What you see of a player is not automatically the whole truth: the less you know him, the wider the estimate.
handbuch.scouting.ablauf:
Hire scouts and give them an assignment with an area, a position or a wanted profile.
An assignment usually runs two weeks, shorter and longer ones are possible. Expenses apply, more abroad.
The report arrives in the inbox.
You reply: keep watching, send on a scouting trip or stop following.
handbuch.scouting.wirkung: The more your scout sees a player live, the more accurate the report. A scouting trip gives a big jump in knowledge but costs about twice the expenses. Your trust in a scout grows when his reports prove right.
handbuch.scouting.mehr:
Three report levels: Rough estimate, Observed and Detailed report. Each level adds more statements about the environment and personality, and accuracy rises.
The environment consists of statements from coaches, team-mates, journalists and agents. Coaches are reliable, agents talk things up, journalists lean negative.
Fit shows in six lights whether a player suits you: position, role, dressing room, wage, style and risk. Secured means CalcioM knows the data, estimated means it rests on your scout's statement. If the basis is missing it says unknown.
Scouts have character: an euphoric one rates too high, a cautious one too low. If two scouts contradict each other, you decide whom to follow.
handbuch.scouting.tipps:
Give scouts areas that suit them. Specialists work faster.
A report with low accuracy is a hint, not a verdict.
As your club's standing grows you may have more scouts and assignments at once.
handbuch.training.kurz: Weekly plan, load, special abilities and retraining.
handbuch.training.was: In the training plan you set what your squad practises during the week. Training makes players better, but it costs energy. More development always means more load.
handbuch.training.ablauf:
Open the training plan. The week has seven days with four slots each: morning, afternoon, evening and individual.
Drag a session onto a slot or tap the session first, then the slot. Choose duration and intensity (light, normal or hard).
Read the week's load light. Green is fine, yellow means some players are running hot, red means too much at once.
Tap Accept week. Only then does the coaching staff get the plan.
At the weekend the training report shows the players who improved.
handbuch.training.wirkung: Young players learn fast, over 29 hardly at all. Individual training, regular appearances and good morale speed up the gain. After an injury a player grows at half speed for three weeks. A strong coaching staff makes every session more useful. Under high load values fade faster and injury risk rises.
handbuch.training.mehr:
Presets: standard week, preparation, match week, regeneration, intensive week and youth focus. You save your own weeks as templates.
On match day only light sessions are allowed, on a rest day only very light ones. The same session several times in a week gives less each time.
Special abilities: on the Special training tab you choose one ability per player to learn. Locked abilities give the reason, for example that he already has it or it does not fit his position. Missing requirements are shown. An experienced mentor raises the chance.
Retraining: the assistant coach suggests players who are needed in a different position. With Take into training the player gets a free individual slot. This takes months. From halfway the new position is decently usable, at the end fully.
handbuch.training.tipps:
Plan light days before matches and use regeneration after hard weeks.
If no individual slot is free, make room on a training day.
Special training and retraining only begin once you have accepted the week.
handbuch.taktik.kurz: Line-up, player suitability and your assistant coach's advice.
handbuch.taktik.was: On the Line-up and tactics page you set formation, starting eleven, style of play, set pieces and penalty takers. Your assistant coach judges who fits where and gives advice.
handbuch.taktik.ablauf:
Choose one of the three tactic slots or create a draft with New tactic.
Choose the formation and fill the positions.
Look at each player's suitability in his position. It shows natural, usable or poor, plus missing values.
Open the assistant coach's advice. Each suggestion names reason, benefit and risk. You can accept, decline or accept all.
On the Opponent instructions tab you decide the mode for the next match.
handbuch.taktik.wirkung: Your team plays what you set at kick-off. Formation and starting eleven give the line-up, the sliders shape the style of play. A player in an unsuitable position stays below his potential.
handbuch.taktik.mehr:
Suitability: natural means it is his main position or he has been retrained there. Usable is a makeshift with a penalty, poor is not worth it. A goalkeeper outfield is always poor.
The mode against the opponent has two choices: Adapt to the opponent or We are stronger: stick to our own game. The assistant coach pre-selects, you can change it. When adapting, the staff prepares adjustments and you decide what goes into the draft.
Suggestions are only as good as your assistant coach. A tactically weak one gives few and cautious advice.
Retraining suggestions appear under the opponent instructions. A training goal only arises from them in training.
Not everything reaches the game. Formation and starting eleven arrive, but for set pieces, penalties and captain some stays in CalcioM only. The page points this out.
handbuch.taktik.tipps:
Read the assistant coach's warnings, for example on missing width or too many attacking roles.
A draft changes nothing until you accept it. Feel free to experiment.
With a strong assistant coach it pays to follow the advice more often.
handbuch.medizin.kurz: Load light, rehab, painkiller shot and your medical department.
handbuch.medizin.was: The Medical page shows injured players, rehab, load and the physios' recommendations. Injuries cost weeks, and anyone who returns too early risks a relapse.
handbuch.medizin.ablauf:
Open Medical and check under Injured who is out and for how long. The duration is a range, not a guarantee.
For longer absences you can start a rehab programme. It costs money but shortens the absence.
Before every match the load light shows who is tired. Red means rotation recommended.
If you want to play an injured player anyway, you are told the relapse risk beforehand and decide.
handbuch.medizin.wirkung: The light weighs tiredness, minutes played, fixture density and proneness. Rehab phases run from treatment via build-up and team training to fit to play. Playing before the end of a phase raises relapse risk sharply. A better medical department reduces injuries, shortens absences and makes forecasts more precise.
handbuch.medizin.mehr:
The painkiller shot makes a player fit at once, for absences up to four weeks and at most three times per season. Afterwards he is very prone to relapse for three weeks and has less fitness and form. Repeated shots can leave lasting damage.
Your medical department consists of doctor, physios, rehab coach and sports scientist plus facilities for rehab, diagnostics and regeneration. A missing post counts as quality zero.
On a transfer there is the medical check. What it means is in the chapter Transfers and negotiation.
handbuch.medizin.tipps:
Rotate in time. Resting red players is cheaper than an absence.
Painkiller shots are for finals, not for everyday use.
Invest in diagnostics if the forecasts are too vague for you.
handbuch.manager.kurz: Your style, courses, leisure and your home.
handbuch.manager.was: You have values too. Leadership, tactical knowledge, authority, media presence, youth work, fitness knowledge and negotiating skill determine how well you work. Add energy, tension, drive and the weight of your word.
handbuch.manager.ablauf:
Open Manager. In the profile you see values, style and private account.
Book a course on the Courses tab. Only one runs at a time, you pay the costs privately.
On the Leisure tab take time for golf, family, friends or a holiday. You have three free evenings per week.
On the Home tab choose how you live.
handbuch.manager.wirkung: Courses raise your values, and coaching licences open bigger clubs. Leisure lowers tension. Anyone burned out works with penalties on all abilities. A better home relieves you week after week.
handbuch.manager.mehr:
You do not choose your style, it arises from your behaviour: tone in conversations, press tones, rotation, tactics and promises kept or broken. There is the Hard One, the Carer, the Diplomat and the Mate. As long as your behaviour is inconsistent it says Still open.
Each style fits player types differently, from the hot-headed to the loyal soul. A good match strengthens your conversations, a bad one weakens them.
Your reputation decides which clubs approach you. In the coach profile you see licences, contract, career and job offers. Offers have deadlines, you can stall at most twice.
Everything here stays in CalcioM, nothing goes into the game.
handbuch.manager.tipps:
Plan courses in quiet weeks, they cost extra energy.
Working nonstop is paid for with penalties. Use the free evenings.
Missing invitations from sponsor or board costs standing.
handbuch.verein.kurz: Stadium, tickets, sponsors, merchandise and money.
handbuch.verein.was: The Finances page and the business centre show what the club earns and spends. You can expand stadium and facilities. The board measures you against expectations and targets.
handbuch.verein.ablauf:
In the business centre look at cash, monthly result, attendance, atmosphere and fan mood.
Change a lever, for example ticket prices, standing places, catering or advertising. You first see a preview with the consequences and then confirm.
For sponsors you pick from offers for shirt, kit supplier and stadium name.
Under Stadium and facilities you expand level by level. You see costs, build time and when the expansion pays off.
handbuch.verein.wirkung: Higher prices bring more money per seat, but less demand and a worse mood. More advertising brings money and costs atmosphere. A good mood fills the stadium and attracts season-ticket buyers. An expansion costs first and pays off later.
handbuch.verein.mehr:
Squad and staff together may cost at most a good three fifths of the expected annual income. Above that new contracts are hard to approve. With too much debt there are no transfers and no expansion.
Normally about half of the surplus goes into the transfer budget. If the board trusts you it is more, with distrust clearly less.
Fan events such as a fan festival, family day or legends match raise mood and media image. After that there is a cooldown.
The board sets season targets. If its trust falls too low it gives you an ultimatum. If you miss it, dismissal looms.
Everything in this chapter only applies in CalcioM and changes no match results in the game.
handbuch.verein.tipps:
Check the preview before you confirm. It also shows attendance and mood.
Sponsor offers only last a few weeks.
With a fan protest a conversation or a lower price usually helps.
handbuch.jugend.kurz: Find, develop, promote or loan out talents.
handbuch.jugend.was: Your academy and the U23 train young players. The youth network helps you find and sign talents in the region.
handbuch.jugend.ablauf:
On the Academy tab divide your talents between academy and U23. The U23 plays in its own league from seven players.
Invest in the youth network in the regions where you want to see talents. With enough network strength they appear in the list.
Build contact, watch a player and sign him. This takes almost a month.
The game suggests good players for promotion. Then a case appears in which you can promote, loan, keep or promise a prospect.
handbuch.jugend.wirkung: Players with appearances and a mentor develop clearly faster than those without match practice. There are peaks and slumps. Anyone promoted counts as part of the first-team squad. Agents and parents react differently to your decision depending on their expectation.
handbuch.jugend.mehr:
A first-team squad has at most 40 and at least 18 players. Academy and U23 together hold at most 40.
You promote in the game via the Sign menu. CalcioM notices it on read-in. Demoting is not possible in the game: CalcioM then lists the player as U23 but does not field him.
A promised prospect is a commitment with a deadline. If you do not keep it, your word suffers.
Loans run six months, with regular feedback.
The youth director matters: the better he is, the faster your network grows.
handbuch.jugend.tipps:
Anyone who does not play learns slowly. Loan out talents if they get no minutes with you.
A mentor must be at least three years older and get on well with the talent.
Nobody signs players while in debt.
handbuch.kabine.kurz: Hierarchy, mood, quarrels and the word you have given.
handbuch.kabine.was: The dressing room is the social fabric of your squad. You see who leads, what the morale is, who gets along with whom, and which promises you have made.
handbuch.kabine.ablauf:
Open the dressing room and look at morale, hierarchy and relationships.
On the Demands and complaints tab read what players want, and reply in the inbox.
If a conflict arises it appears as a case. You choose how to step in.
If needed, name captain and vice-captain. You award the armband in the game yourself.
Before the match you give a speech or consciously say nothing.
handbuch.kabine.wirkung: Good morale helps learning and form. Unhappy players voice a transfer request, and spokesmen can carry the dressing room with them. Promises kept strengthen trust, promises broken weigh heavier than an honest refusal.
handbuch.kabine.mehr:
Promises arise from conversations: playing time, role, contract, wage or release. Each has a deadline, about four weeks for playing time and role. A playing-time promise counts as kept if the player starts afterwards. You see all of them on the Promises tile.
Conflicts come as quarrels, split groups, a wobbling captain and signings who have not settled in. Depending on the measure the chances of settling it differ greatly. Punishment rarely helps, letting it run almost never.
Discipline: for lateness or criticism you choose between leniency, a warning, a fine and the bench. Anyone who spares regulars and punishes others risks team spirit.
Speeches work depending on the score: encouragement helps when behind, hardness rather not when ahead.
handbuch.kabine.tipps:
Only give promises you can keep.
Treat players equally. Unequal punishments cost team spirit.
A short, honest refusal is better than a broken promise.
handbuch.medien.kurz: What you say is in the paper tomorrow.
handbuch.medien.was: The press follows every match. In the press conference you answer journalists' questions. Your tone shapes how people report about you and the club.
handbuch.medien.ablauf:
The conference is due from the day before the match and runs two more days afterwards. You find it in the inbox and under Press.
The press officer opens, then journalists ask four questions.
Choose a tone for each question. The preview shows the effect beforehand.
At the end the headline of tomorrow appears. The next day the articles are in the papers.
handbuch.medien.wirkung: Your tones change media image, board trust, fan mood and morale. Honest and diplomatic bring trust, confident brings fans, criticising the team costs morale, evading harms the media image. Anyone who does not show up loses standing.
handbuch.medien.mehr:
Journalists have styles: factual, tabloid, benevolent, critical. Each answer shifts how well disposed they are toward you. If they like your tone, it has a stronger effect.
The size of the outlet counts: a global brand has far more effect than a small paper.
Rumours you can deny, confirm or not comment on. A refuted denial hurts.
In the game world settings you can let the press officer answer or switch conferences off altogether.
Fan voices show messages from fans, ultras and pundits. With a bad mood come whistles and protests.
handbuch.medien.tipps:
Pick the tone that fits the situation. After a defeat honesty is usually safe.
Your press style also rubs off on your manager style.
Good relations with journalists pay off in bad times.
handbuch.zeitung.kurz: Der Sportbote tells your season, the diary records it.
handbuch.zeitung.was: The newspaper is called Der Sportbote. It appears daily or weekly and reports on your club. The diary collects everything you experience on a timeline.
handbuch.zeitung.ablauf:
Open Newspaper. The front page shows the main story, further stories, a ticker and transfer rumours.
In the archive you browse earlier issues.
Open Diary. The timeline is organised by season, month and entry. Open an entry to see line-up, statistics and scorers.
On the Season history tab you compare all seasons side by side.
handbuch.zeitung.wirkung: The newspaper reflects what happened and what you said at press conferences. It changes nothing in the game, but it brings your story to life. The diary records matches, moments, transfers, injuries, awards and titles.
handbuch.zeitung.mehr:
The paper's tone follows the situation: after a thrashing, a losing streak or a hat-trick it turns tabloid. A breaking-news item appears for a dismissal, ultimatum, sale of a key player or serious injury.
Transfer rumours develop as a story in several parts from rumour to outcome.
Moments in the diary arise by themselves: hat-trick, thrashing, winning streak, losing streak or conquered top spot.
The diary fills with the first week played.
handbuch.zeitung.tipps:
A press conference with a clear tone ends up as a quote in the paper the next day.
Use the filter in the diary to see only transfers or injuries.
handbuch.saisonende.kurz: Review, honours and farewell to the season.
handbuch.saisonende.was: On the last matchday the chairman sends you the season wrap-up: final table, season target, review, honours and farewells. The season then moves into the archive.
handbuch.saisonende.ablauf:
Read the season wrap-up in the inbox. It stays available for a few weeks.
Open the Diary, tab Season history, for record and goals of each season.
Under Rankings look for the best of the month and season and the golden boot.
There you also see squad strength, standing and record transfers.
handbuch.saisonende.wirkung: The wrap-up tells how the season went relative to your season target: title, target reached, narrowly missed or missed. It changes nothing itself. Honours appear in the player profile, as a headline and in the diary.
handbuch.saisonende.mehr:
Awarded are Player of the month, Team of the week, Player of the season, Best young player, Ballon d'Or and Goal of the season. Each honour gives its reasons in numbers. Young means 21 at most.
For the Goal of the season CalcioM says honestly what it knows: the game keeps no individual goals, so the top-scorer moment counts.
Manager of the month is whoever gets the most points per match with his team.
Rankings only show what is known. If a number is missing, so is the sentence about it.
handbuch.saisonende.tipps:
The review also shows contracts that expire within the next twelve months.
Use the wrap-up to plan targets for the next season.
handbuch.einstellungen.kurz: How much you decide yourself and what your staff takes over.
handbuch.einstellungen.was: Under Rules and customisation you decide for each system of your career whether you decide yourself, your staff takes over or it does not run at all. The options, by contrast, only control the interface.
handbuch.einstellungen.ablauf:
Open Rules and customisation. At the top are the presets, below one card per system.
Pick a preset or switch a system individually: You decide, Your staff takes over or Does not run.
Before it applies, a window shows what changes.
In the options you set size, accent colour, motion, language, sound and display.
handbuch.einstellungen.wirkung: Realistic is the full game, you decide everywhere yourself. Comfort lets the staff take over routine cases, important decisions stay with you. Sandbox is for trying things out: happy players, open budget, no injuries. A career that ever ran in sandbox mode stays marked as a sandbox career.
handbuch.einstellungen.mehr:
There are systems for demands, morale, training, injuries, contracts, scouting, finances, press, discipline and youth. Line-up and transfers only know yourself or staff and cannot be switched off.
If you change one system individually, the preset is called Own rules afterwards.
The Beginner display shows stars and lights, Pro shows numbers, ranges and drivers.
For press the press officer can answer or conferences are dropped altogether.
handbuch.einstellungen.tipps:
When in doubt start with Realistic or Comfort.
Sandbox is never preselected.
The interface size takes effect at once and is remembered.
